\chapter{Chapter02 — Majority Optimality}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter02.TotalInfluence.MajorityOptimality}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[First coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.firstCoordinateRestriction}
\label{FABL.firstCoordinateRestriction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional
cube, and fix $b\in\{\pm1\}$. The restriction of $f$ to the slice whose first coordinate
is $b$ is the function on the $n$-dimensional cube given by $x\mapsto f(b,x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a uniform random sign]
\lean{FABL.expect_sign}
\label{FABL.expect_sign}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{4}
For every function $g:\{−1,1\}\to\mathbb R$, its uniform mean over the two signs is
$\mathbb E_b[g(b)]=(g(1)+g(-1))/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign cube average by first coordinate]
\lean{FABL.expect_fin_cons}
\label{FABL.expect_fin_cons}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.expect_sign}
\difficulty{4}
For every function $h:\{-1,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, its uniform average over the sign
cube equals half the sum of its uniform averages on the two slices with first coordinate
$1$ and $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence under coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.booleanInfluence_succ}
\label{FABL.booleanInfluence_succ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsPivotal, FABL.booleanInfluence, FABL.expect_fin_cons, FABL.firstCoordinateRestriction, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the
$(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube, and let $i$ be a coordinate among the last $n$
coordinates. The influence of that coordinate equals the average of its influences in
the two restrictions of $f$ obtained by fixing the first coordinate to $1$ and to $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence of the first coordinate]
\lean{FABL.booleanInfluence_zero}
\label{FABL.booleanInfluence_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsPivotal, FABL.booleanInfluence, FABL.expect_fin_cons, FABL.firstCoordinateRestriction, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the
$(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube. Its influence at the first coordinate equals the
probability, for a uniformly chosen sign vector $x$ of length $n$, that the two
functions obtained by fixing the first coordinate of $f$ to $1$ and to $-1$ take
different values at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total influence under first-coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_cons}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_cons}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.booleanInfluence_eq_influence_toReal, FABL.booleanInfluence_succ, FABL.booleanInfluence_zero, FABL.firstCoordinateRestriction, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a function from the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign
cube to $\\{ -1,1 \\}$. The total influence of the real-valued function obtained from
$f$ equals the average of the total influences of its two restrictions to the first
coordinate, plus the uniform probability that these restrictions disagree.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ agree with the sign of $\\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$ at every
input $x$ for which this sum is nonzero; its values when the sum is zero may be
arbitrary. Then $f$ is monotone in the coordinatewise order $-1<1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Lifted odd majority]
\lean{FABL.liftedOddMajority}

\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Influence under lifted odd majority]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_liftedOddMajority}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_liftedOddMajority}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.liftedOddMajority, FABL.majority, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_cons, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $m$, the total influence of odd majority on $2m+1$ coordinates
is equal to the total influence of the function on $2m+2$ coordinates obtained by
applying odd majority to the last $2m+1$ coordinates and ignoring the first coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a monotone Boolean function on
$\\{-1,1\\}^n$. Its total influence equals the sum of its Fourier coefficients indexed
by singleton coordinate sets: $\\operatorname{Inf}_{\\mathrm{tot}}(f)=\\sum_{i=1}^n
\\widehat f(\\{i\\})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Agreeing vote count]
\lean{FABL.agreeingVoteCount}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p050-b005}
\label{FABL.agreeingVoteCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube to the
signs, and let $x$ be an element of that cube. The agreeing vote count of $f$ at $x$ is
the number of coordinates $i$ for which the sign $x_i$ equals $f(x)$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$. The number
of coordinates $i$ for which $x_i=f(x)$ equals
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{1+f(x)x_i}{2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

coefficients of $f$ indexed by the singleton coordinate sets equals the uniform average
over $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ of $f(x)$ times the sum of the coordinates of $x$.

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. The uniform average
over $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ of the number of coordinates $i$ for which $x_i=f(x)$ is $\frac
n2+\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat f(\{i\})$, where $\widehat f(\{i\})$ is the Fourier
coefficient of the real-valued sign function $f$ at the singleton $\{i\}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$.
Write $M(x)=1$ if $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge0$ and $M(x)=-1$ otherwise. Then $f(x)\sum_{i=1}^n
x_i\le M(x)\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. The sum of the singleton
Fourier coefficients of $f$ is at most the sum of the singleton Fourier coefficients of
majority, where majority is $+1$ when the coordinate sum is nonnegative and $-1$
otherwise.

  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p051-b002}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Define majority to be
$+1$ when the sum of the coordinates is nonnegative and $-1$ otherwise. The sum of the
singleton Fourier coefficients of $f$ equals that of majority if and only if $f(x)$
agrees with majority at every $x$ whose coordinate sum is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every $n\ge 0$ and every coordinatewise monotone sign-valued Boolean function $f$ on
the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, the total influence of its real-valued version is at
most the total influence of majority on that cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total influence of majority functions]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_eq_majority_of_isMajorityFunction}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_eq_majority_of_isMajorityFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsMajorityFunction, FABL.IsMajorityFunction.monotone, FABL.majority, FABL.majority_monotone, FABL.sum_fourierCoeff_singleton_eq_majority_iff, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_eq_sum_fourierCoeff_singleton_of_monotone}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a Boolean function on $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ that
agrees with the sign of the sum of the input coordinates whenever that sum is nonzero.
Then $f$ and the majority function have equal total influence.
\end{theorem}
